newsitem.title: JAPAN: OLYMPICS-LOTTERY SET UP TO COPE WITH DEMAND FOR GAMES TICKETS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-LOTTERY SET UP TO COPE WITH DEMAND FOR GAMES TICKETS.

text.p: Some tickets for next year's Winter Olympics will be distributed by lottery after huge numbers of applications, organisers said on Wednesday.
The lottery would cover 366,000 tickets earmarked for domestic sales, organising chief Makoto Kobayashi said.

He said organisers had received nearly 290,000 application letters postmarked by the March 14 deadline. Each applicant could request up to eight tickets so the total number of requests could exceed two million.
"Of course, were really happy that people are interested in applying for tickets for the Games," he added. "We were actually surprised there were so many applications."
Kobayashi said the most-requested events would not be known until the end of March, when the applications had been processed.
Applicants could request only two tickets to the opening and closing ceremonies, the figure skating exhibition and the final rounds of the men's hockey.
Successful applicants would be notified in May, he said.
About 1.28 million tickets are available for the Nagano Games, with prices ranging from 2,000 yen ($17) to 35,000 yen ($300).
